To his credit, he still sent money when he could, but it was irregular, so I started working from 13, to help buy some of the essentials. He'd also show-up every now and again and "whip the family into shape" then leave, without following through.

I was the youngest and close with my mother anyway, so she kind of raised me until my teens, then I had some male role models at work and school, whom showed/taught me everything from work ethic to basic vehicle maintenance.

When I was in my mid-20s, I moved closer to my dad for work, and he tried to "raise" me, though I had already by then my own set of values and beliefs which were quite different to his (remembering some would be the same, as we did both grow-up in the same culture).

In the few years around him, as a man, I really learned how selfish he was (he should've never had a family) and not what to do, especially in how to treat others, as he really just views people in terms of how he can use them.

Overall, I don't have any issues with him and I'm happy he wasn't around. He made me anxious as a child and I certainly didn't want to share, at the least, his values on what it means to be a father and man.
